# Draw an office: Modern office, cutaway

<!-- Generated by tools/office-prompt/build.mjs from docs/office-svg/spec.json and assets/cut/modern/. Do not edit; edit the spec or the symbols. -->

Copy everything below the line into your AI assistant, then describe the office you want. Paste the SVG it returns into the office builder. If the builder lists problems, paste the list back to the assistant and ask it to fix them.

---

You are drawing a virtual office as a single SVG file for a product that places people's avatars into rooms. Output one complete SVG and nothing else: no explanation, no markdown fence. Before you draw, ask me these and wait for my answers: how many people the office is for; which rooms I want and what they are called; landscape, square or portrait; light only, or light and dark.

## The structure (required)

The product reads the rooms out of the file, so the structure is a contract. Follow it exactly.

- Root: `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="…" data-ofis="1" data-canvas="…" data-avatar="small">`. The viewBox is one of: landscape (16:9, viewBox="0 0 1920 1080"), square (1:1, viewBox="0 0 1080 1080"), portrait (3:4, viewBox="0 0 1080 1440"). `data-canvas` names the one you used.
- Direct children, in order: `<defs>` (the symbols below, copied verbatim), `<g id="backdrop">` (everything that is not a room and sits below the rooms: sky, ground, the building shell, floor slabs), `<g id="rooms">` (the room groups), and optionally `<g id="overlay">` (optional: anything drawn above the rooms, such as pillars between them).
- A room is `<g id="room-<type>-<Name>" data-bar="top">` inside `#rooms`. Type is one of reception, break, workspace, meeting, conference. Name is the room's display name with underscores for spaces, for example `room-meeting-Design_studio`. `data-bar` is top or bottom: which edge the product's 32px control bar sits on. Keep that edge calm.
- The first `<rect>` inside a room group is the room's bounds, read from its x, y, width and height. Everything inside the room goes inside its group.
- Where people stand: `<rect id="area-4x1" x="…" y="…" width="…" height="…" fill="none"/>` inside the room, a child of the room group; its x and y are the area's top-left corner. `area-<columns>x<rows>` says how many avatars fit. One cell in viewBox pixels: landscape: small 90×120, medium 120×161.25, large 165×213.75; square: small 67.5×90, medium 90×120.9375, large 123.75×160.3125; portrait: small 90×120, medium 120×161.25, large 165×213.75. The area must be invisible (fill="none" and no stroke, so it never shows in the picture) and must lie inside the room, below the top 32px bar strip (or above the bottom one), clear of furniture that stands where people would.

## The rules (the product refuses a file that breaks one)

- Exactly one reception and exactly one break room.
- Room names are unique within the file.
- Rooms do not overlap; every room lies inside the canvas.
- A room is wide enough for its control bar (168px at a 1024x768 viewport) and tall enough for the bar plus one avatar cell.
- Every area lies inside its room, clear of the bar edge and of other areas.
- No lettering anywhere: no <text>. The product draws every room name on the room's bar.
- No animation. Office pictures are still.
- The dark variant has identical structure and geometry to the light one; only colours differ.
- At most 30 rooms. Every room at least 168px wide at a 1024px-wide viewport (about 315px on the landscape and portrait viewBoxes, 237px on the square one) and tall enough for the bar plus one cell.
- Allowed elements: svg, g, defs, symbol, use, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path, title, desc, metadata, linearGradient, radialGradient, stop, pattern, clipPath, mask, marker, switch, style, filter, feBlend, feColorMatrix, feComponentTransfer, feFuncA, feFuncB, feFuncG, feFuncR, feComposite, feDropShadow, feFlood, feGaussianBlur, feMerge, feMergeNode, feMorphology, feOffset, feTurbulence, feDisplacementMap, feDiffuseLighting, feSpecularLighting, feDistantLight, fePointLight, feSpotLight.
- Refused: <script> (runs code), <foreignObject> (embeds a document), <image> (embeds a raster image; draw everything as shapes), <a> (is a link), <animate> (animates), <animateTransform> (animates), <animateMotion> (animates), <set> (animates), DOCTYPE (declarations are not read at all).
- No on* event attributes.
- href and xlink:href may only point at an id in the same file (#…).
- style attributes and <style> blocks may not use url() to anything but an id, @import, or expression().

## How to draw (cutaway)

- The office is a building seen in cutaway, like a dollhouse with the front wall removed. Rooms sit on levels: rooms in one row share a y and a height, with a `<use href="#floor">` slab under the row in `#backdrop` and a `<use href="#pillar">` between neighbours in `#overlay`.
- Draw the building shell (roof, outer wall, plinth) and whatever is outside it in `#backdrop`. Each room group starts with its back-wall rect, then its furniture standing on the floor line.
- Furniture is the layout. Draw chairs, desks and tables so an empty room still looks furnished.
- Leave the floor in front of furniture clear where avatars will stand; the area marker says where.
- Nothing tall on a desk or table surface, and a calm wall behind each seat, so a face and a name label read against it.
- Keep contrast moderate: the product draws room bars and status dots on top in both light and dark, and they have to win.
- No people, no faces, no logos, no brands.
- Place symbols with `<use href="#id" x="…" y="…"/>`. Do not redraw them; the theme is the symbols.

## The Modern office symbols, cutaway (copy this `<defs>` block verbatim)

Available: `#art` (a wall picture), `#bookshelf` (a wall-standing shelf), `#cafe` (a round café table on one stem; its x is its centre), `#chair` (a chair, drawn from the front; its x is its centre), `#clock` (wall-mounted; its x, y is its centre), `#counter` (a reception counter), `#desk` (a desk, surface clear; put a chair in front of it), `#floor` (a level slab spanning the building, placed at the bottom of a row of rooms), `#kitchen` (a kitchen run for the break room), `#lamp` (a hanging lamp with a glow; y is the ceiling), `#pillar` (a divider between two rooms on the same level; goes in #overlay), `#plant` (a floor plant; its x is its centre, y its base), `#rug` (a rug on the floor line; its x is its centre), `#sofa` (a sofa for a lounge, library or café), `#stool` (a stool for a café table; its x is its centre), `#table` (a long table for a meeting room; chairs along the front), `#tallplant` (a tall floor plant; its x is its centre, y its base), `#whiteboard` (wall-mounted), `#window` (wall-mounted).

## A worked skeleton (two rooms; yours will have more)

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" width="1920" height="1080" data-ofis="1" data-canvas="landscape" data-avatar="small" data-name="Two rooms">
  <defs>
    <!-- Paste a theme's symbols and gradients here. -->
  </defs>
  <g id="backdrop">
    <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#e9eef3"/>
    <rect x="100" y="60" width="1720" height="980" fill="#efe7db" stroke="#a9998a" stroke-width="8"/>
  </g>
  <g id="rooms">
    <g id="room-reception-Reception" data-bar="top">
      <rect x="100" y="742" width="500" height="298" fill="#fbf1d6"/>
      <use href="#counter" x="140" y="970"/>
      <use href="#plant" x="560" y="1002"/>
      <rect id="area-4x1" x="192" y="832" width="360" height="120" fill="none"/>
    </g>
    <g id="room-break-Cafe" data-bar="top">
      <rect x="1264" y="742" width="556" height="298" fill="#e3ece2"/>
      <use href="#kitchen" x="1294" y="862"/>
      <use href="#sofa" x="1354" y="986"/>
      <rect id="area-4x1" x="1363" y="842" width="360" height="120" fill="none"/>
    </g>
  </g>
  <g id="overlay">
    <use href="#pillar" x="600" y="742"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```

A complete example office drawn with these symbols is in the ofiskit repository at docs/office-svg/examples/modern-cutaway-landscape.svg; edit from it rather than composing from nothing if you can read files.
